tasks.short: Design and implement warehouse strategies for production materials and finished goods.

steps.what: Export inventory, movement and location records for warehouse planning.
Walk the warehouse with supervisors to verify constraints and handling problems.
Compare storage, replenishment and picking options against capacity, service and cost.
Discuss operational tradeoffs with warehouse, production and safety representatives.
Write the investment request, pilot scope and rollout milestones.
Approve investment, operational disruption and pilot limits.
Set pilot locations, replenishment parameters and handling rules in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Review pilot results and decide whether to expand, change or stop.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads the {OPS_SYSTEM}, checks data quality and calculates warehouse scenarios using explicit capacity and cost constraints. A template generator produces the rollout proposal in {DOCS}, while configured pilot controls in the {OPS_SYSTEM} feed a results dashboard in {BI}. People verify physical constraints, choose the strategy and approve operational changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Movement data, physical constraints and cost assumptions were maintained separately. Bespoke scenario calculations and connections were costly to build and maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, planning configuration and deterministic optimisation cover much of the preparation. AI coding can reduce implementation effort without changing the underlying planning methods.
tasks.still_hard: Congestion, safe handling and disruption during change need site knowledge. Inaccurate movement records or unrealistic assumptions can make a mathematically sound scenario impractical.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising unsafe or unworkable layouts and balancing service, investment and disruption with the people running the warehouse.

ambition.what: Monthly warehouse capacity and slotting adjustment decisions

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling comparisons and more time testing operational choices on site. They can gain delegated authority to adjust slotting within approved capacity, safety and spending limits.

reach.task: Build and validate warehouse capacity scenarios.
reach.learn: Constraint modelling, sensitivity analysis and validation against observed warehouse performance.

reach.task: Assess how material replenishment changes affect production schedules.
reach.learn: Production sequencing, material availability and replenishment lead times.

evidence.claim: Inventory planning software can calculate forecasts and stock settings; this supports replenishment analysis, not complete warehouse strategy design.
Lasaulec reported stock reductions above 20% and availability above 98%; the vendor case does not establish the same result for warehouse redesign.
Deterministic scenario calculations and template generation can reduce preparation while physical feasibility and investment decisions remain human.

assumptions: The first release covers one warehouse and existing handling equipment.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
The consultation and access range includes a national-rules assessment and employee consultation if operational changes require it.
Capacity modelling uses aggregate operational data rather than individual worker scoring.
unknowns: Availability and quality of movement timestamps, dimensions and location capacities.
Supported exports and configuration interfaces in the installed {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Local approval limits for investment and warehouse changes.
Applicable national rules and existing employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which existing planning functions can replace custom scenario code?
How well do historical scenarios reproduce observed congestion and service levels?
Which physical constraints must be recorded before a scenario can be considered feasible?
new_work: Maintain capacity, handling-cost and safety constraints.
Resolve missing dimensions and inconsistent movement records.
Check pilot outcomes against scenario assumptions.
Maintain integrations and review proposed configuration changes.

tasks.short: Design and oversee product take-back programmes for reuse, recycling and responsible disposal.

steps.what: Review returned-product volumes, reasons and recovery outcomes in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Check product obligations, handling restrictions and permitted recovery routes.
Compare collection, inspection, reuse, recycling and disposal programme options.
Negotiate partner responsibilities, acceptance criteria, capacity and evidence requirements.
Draft the programme instructions, escalation rules and business case.

loop.input: Approved disposition constraints, proposed partner terms, scenario figures and programme template.
loop.output: Draft programme instructions and business case with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require references for obligations and partner terms; reconcile every figure with the scenario table.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per proposal; leave unsupported sections blank for human completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Partner responsibilities and operating instructions arrive as varied prose; calculations and fixed sections remain deterministic.

steps.what: Approve programme scope, spending and partner commitments.
Configure return categories, routing rules and inspection checkpoints in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Match partner recovery receipts to returned quantities and report missing evidence.
Resolve uncertain dispositions and authorise exceptional disposal instructions.

tasks.design: Configured return routes in the {OPS_SYSTEM} use approved product and disposition rules, while a deterministic service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} compares programme options and reconciles partner receipts. A bounded drafting loop prepares instructions in {DOCS} from approved constraints and partner terms. People approve commitments and exceptional dispositions, with evidence gaps tracked in the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Return records, partner evidence and product-specific obligations were disconnected. Changing partner formats and uncertain product condition made full automation unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured return workflows and deterministic quantity reconciliation handle stable parts of the programme. Bounded drafting can turn approved material into usable instructions without delegating legal interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Product condition, waste classification and partner evidence can remain uncertain. Sector, cross-border and national rules require specialist interpretation; customer return data also brings GDPR duties.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing defensible recovery routes when value, safety, environmental outcomes and partner capability conflict.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconciling receipts and rewriting instructions, and more time developing recovery partnerships. They can gain authority to pilot a spare-parts recovery channel within approved compliance and spending limits.

reach.task: Define inspection and acceptance criteria for recovered products.
reach.learn: Condition grading, traceability and evidence needed before reuse.

reach.task: Design collection and consolidation routes for returned goods.
reach.learn: Reverse-flow economics, transport restrictions and partner capacity planning.

evidence.claim: Configured routing, deterministic reconciliation and human disposition approvals form a feasible programme design; the digest provides no direct reverse-logistics implementation case.
A bounded model loop can draft instructions from approved source material, but cannot establish whether a recovery route is legally permitted.
GDPR obligations apply when return records contain personal data; sector and national rules depend on the programme.

assumptions: The first release covers one product family and a small set of recovery partners.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Structured partner receipts are used initially; unsupported documents go to manual review.
The consultation and access range includes partner data agreements, GDPR assessment and national employee consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Products, jurisdictions and waste categories covered by the programme.
Partner permits, contractual responsibilities and evidence formats.
Whether returned products retain reliable identifiers through recovery.
Actual recovery value, inspection cost and customer uptake.
Applicable national rules and consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which return routes can be configured directly in the existing {OPS_SYSTEM}?
Which evidence proves physical recovery rather than only partner receipt?
What identifiers and quantity tolerances support reliable reconciliation?
Which product conditions always require specialist disposition approval?
new_work: Review unsupported draft instructions and changed partner terms.
Resolve missing receipts and quantity mismatches.
Maintain permitted routes, partner permits and acceptance criteria.
Audit recovery evidence and investigate exceptional dispositions.
Maintain integrations and access controls for customer return data.

tasks.short: Develop and implement supplier evaluation and selection procedures.

steps.what: Export supplier delivery, quality and purchasing performance from the {PROCUREMENT}.
Review supplier questionnaires, certificates and audit findings for usable evaluation evidence.

loop.input: Supplier questionnaires, certificates and audit reports, linked to supplier identifiers.
loop.output: Proposed evidence fields with document references, expiry dates and explicit missing values.
loop.check: Validate field types, supplier identity and dates; require a source passage and reviewer acceptance for material fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unreadable, conflicting or unsupported fields enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative audit findings and varying document layouts require interpretation; structured questionnaire fields use direct mapping.

steps.what: Agree evaluation criteria, weights, disqualifiers and exception responsibilities with stakeholders.
Build the supplier scorecard and its scoring formulas.
Test the method against previous awards, missing evidence and alternative weights.
Approve the evaluation policy, escalation thresholds and required award approvals.
Configure evaluation forms, scoring rules and approval routing in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Review pilot recommendations and decide whether the evaluation method needs changes.

tasks.design: Configure supplier forms, deterministic scoring and approval routing in the {PROCUREMENT}, with a bounded extraction loop for narrative evidence held in {DOCS}. A service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} generates scorecards and sensitivity tests, with results shown in {BI}. People approve criteria, material evidence and policy changes; supplier awards retain their required approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered across supplier documents and performance exports. Scorecards were easy to create but hard to validate, version and connect to approval processes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing evaluation configuration handles structured criteria and routing. Deterministic generators and bounded document extraction can reduce assembly work while preserving evidence references.
tasks.still_hard: Weights encode business priorities and can conceal weak evidence. Historical awards are comparison cases, not proof of the correct decision; new suppliers may lack comparable performance data.
tasks.human_edge: Judging strategic dependence, credible improvement plans and risks that a weighted score cannot settle.

ambition.what: An evidence-based qualification route for small suppliers without delivery history

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time constructing scorecards and more time challenging evidence and testing selection rules. They can gain authority to sponsor a controlled qualification route for new suppliers, while award authority remains with the designated approver.

reach.task: Validate supplier quality evidence and qualification thresholds.
reach.learn: Audit evidence, certificate scope and the difference between missing evidence and failed requirements.

reach.task: Test score sensitivity and compare alternative evaluation methods.
reach.learn: Weight sensitivity, missing-data treatment and validation without copying historical biases.

evidence.claim: Configured evaluation forms, deterministic scoring and sensitivity tests can support supplier-method design without autonomous selection.
Bounded extraction can propose fields from supplier documents, with source checks and human acceptance for material evidence.
The digest contains no direct case proving this supplier evaluation design or its estimated time savings.

assumptions: The first release covers one purchasing category.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The installed {PROCUREMENT} supports configurable evaluation forms and approval routing.
The consultation and access range includes confidential-document access, GDPR review for personal data and national consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Where delivery and quality performance records are actually held.
Which evaluation functions are licensed and available in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Existing procurement approval limits and mandatory qualification requirements.
Supplier document quality, languages and permitted reuse.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which criteria are genuine disqualifiers rather than weighted preferences?
How sensitive are rankings to weights, missing evidence and uncertain measurements?
Which document fields can use direct mapping instead of a model loop?
How should new suppliers demonstrate capability without historical performance?
new_work: Review extracted evidence and conflicting supplier claims.
Maintain criteria versions, scoring rules and approval routes.
Investigate unstable rankings and recurring overrides.
Review certificate expiry and evidence freshness.
Maintain document access controls and extraction checks.

tasks.short: Document supply chain workflows, cycle times, responsibilities and system flows.

steps.what: Agree the process scope, intended readers and responsible process owner.
Observe physical work and ask operators about handoffs, exceptions and actual responsibilities.
Export relevant transactions and timestamps from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Calculate cycle times and distinguish processing, waiting and missing timestamps.
Draw process flows and write responsibilities, system handoffs and exception instructions.

loop.input: Scoped observation notes, validated cycle-time figures and existing procedure sections.
loop.output: Draft process graph, responsibility table and procedure with source references and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate graph structure, references, role names and exact reuse of calculated figures; flag unsupported transitions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per process; unresolved roles or transitions remain marked for the walkthrough.
loop.why_not_simpler: Observation notes describe varied sequences and exceptions in prose; diagram rendering and numerical tables remain deterministic.

steps.what: Walk through the draft with operators and correct missing steps or disputed responsibilities.
Approve and publish the controlled procedure with its owner and review date.

tasks.design: A deterministic service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads scoped events from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and calculates cycle-time tables. A bounded drafting loop combines those tables with observation notes, then a deterministic renderer produces diagrams and procedures in {DOCS}. Configured document approval and versioning publish the procedure after an operator walkthrough and process-owner approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical observations and transaction logs rarely formed one consistent record. Writing, drawing and maintaining documents required substantial manual effort even when the underlying process was understood.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can turn notes into a structured first version, while ordinary code calculates metrics and renders diagrams. Existing document controls handle approval and versioning.
tasks.still_hard: Event logs show recorded transactions, not every physical step or actual responsibility. Undocumented workarounds require observation; worker-identifiable logs need GDPR controls and assessment under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Discovering what people actually do and resolving disagreement about handoffs, responsibility and safe exceptions.

ambition.what: A verified process handover pack for temporary warehouse teams

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time formatting procedures and more time observing work and resolving unclear handoffs. They can take responsibility for cross-team documentation readiness; operational change authority does not automatically change.

reach.task: Map process variation and identify bottlenecks.
reach.learn: Event definitions, observation methods and separating measured delay from incomplete logging.

reach.task: Validate receipt, movement and inventory exception instructions.
reach.learn: Frontline transaction sequences, practical checks and common workarounds.

evidence.claim: Event calculations, diagram rendering and document publication can use deterministic code and existing configuration.
A bounded drafting loop can structure observation notes, but operator validation is needed before treating the result as the actual process.
The digest provides no documented case establishing the proposed documentation savings.
Worker-identifiable operational logs require GDPR controls; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the intended use.

assumptions: The first release covers one process with accessible transaction timestamps.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Observation notes are collected directly; recording and transcription are outside the initial scope.
The consultation and access range includes event-data access and any required consultation about worker-identifiable logs.
Calculated metrics describe process performance rather than individual worker rankings.
unknowns: Whether timestamps reflect physical activity or delayed data entry.
Availability of stable transaction identifiers and event definitions.
Current document approval and version-control capabilities.
Whether observation notes or logs contain personal data.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which physical steps are absent from transaction records?
Which timing measures remain reliable after missing and delayed entries are excluded?
Can each generated transition and responsibility be traced to an observation or approved source?
What operational changes should trigger a procedure review?
new_work: Resolve unsupported transitions and conflicting observation notes.
Maintain event definitions, templates and diagram checks.
Track procedure ownership, review dates and superseded versions.
Maintain data minimisation and access rules for operational logs.

role.altitude: The supply chain manager's week shifts from assembling records and documents toward site validation, scenario choices, partner discussions and controlled pilots. Delegated rights can expand for bounded operational experiments; investment, supplier commitments and regulated dispositions still follow named approval limits.
reach: Logistics Analysts: validate capacity, recovery-cost and service scenarios.
Quality Control Systems Managers: connect supplier and returned-product evidence to acceptance criteria.
Management Analysts: test evaluation methods and interpret process variation.
Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks: connect warehouse changes to material availability and production schedules.
skills_to_grow: Operational data quality and event definitions
Supplier evidence evaluation and missing-data treatment
Reverse logistics economics and compliance boundaries
Process observation and clear technical writing
Configuration, integration ownership and bounded model validation
role.ambitious_version: Run a supply chain improvement service that offers monthly warehouse capacity decisions, a controlled spare-parts recovery channel and evidence-based qualification for small suppliers. Use shared operational records and explicit approval limits to turn tested ideas into practical changes across warehouse, purchasing and recovery teams.
